search.initial_condition: nominal motors, fully inverted, flat ground

interpretation: All 192 active-controller worlds acquire at least one distal contact and none crosses a joint limit. Contact acquisition does not establish continuous support, useful contact force or qualified recovery.
No world has upright dwell. All 224 are valid performance failures and the unchanged five-degree gain screen returns no leads.

Maximum rotation is 14.2349278911 degrees for unchanged base profiles, 14.2724739977 for root-pivot targets, and 14.2724740249 for torso-edge targets. The fresh timed maximum is 14.3705209804 degrees.

Across the 64 matched groups, mean peak-rotation change from each unchanged base profile is 2.71082957748 degrees for root targets and 2.9518781167 for torso-edge targets. These are descriptive finite comparisons, not a fitted selector or qualification.
The full route verifies both pivot paths, measured contact, bounded pushes, anchors, sweeps and new cycles. Broad compact reading verifies outcomes without claiming full controller-decision replay.
The next contact-envelope analysis is a geometry and controller-design hypothesis. This result does not prove physical impossibility or justify relaxing joint, force or qualification limits.
next_gate: Quantify the reachable contact envelope from compiled body and joint geometry before choosing another controller. Use the retained measured poses and projection residuals to separate unreachable virtual targets from loss of physical contact. Search broad factored body/pose proposals with unchanged joint and force bounds, then prospectively declare a complete gate, small full route and fresh native cohort for useful diverse candidates. Geometric feasibility alone is not dynamic feasibility; useful native leads still need fresh full-capture varied-start confirmation before the same-body Studio handoff.
